diagram_math_checks.objects: For every fixed tau>0, S_tau is the scalar map R to R defined on lines 29–30. The horizontal coordinate is z and the vertical coordinate is S_tau(z); one coordinate unit on either axis represents tau.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The explicit positive-tau hypothesis permits the common rescaling z=tau*x, S_tau(z)=tau*y.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The segment from (-1,0) to (1,0) represents S_tau(z)=0 for -tau<=z<=tau, including both endpoints.
diagram_math_checks.justification: This is exactly the middle branch at line 30. Filled points at the two thresholds agree with that branch.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The left ray through (-1,0) and (-3.2,-2.2) has equation y=x+1 and the right ray through (1,0) and (3.2,2.2) has equation y=x-1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: After the stated common tau rescaling these are S_tau(z)=z+tau for z<-tau and S_tau(z)=z-tau for z>tau, the last and first branches at line 30. Both slopes are one, and arrows point outward to indicate continuation.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Each outer branch has limit zero at its adjacent threshold; the drawing joins each ray to the closed zero segment.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Substitution into the two affine formulas gives (-tau)+tau=0 and tau-tau=0. No relation beyond the given formula is assumed; the complete definition remains independent of the figure.
